_comment: Production behaviour (PLAN.md section 9): Iceberg maintenance, freshness SLAs per data product, late EDR reprocess, clock-skew tolerance. Table names are <layer>.<table> under the rsingh_evx_ prefix. Business dates are decoupled from the wall clock (PLAN section 15); every calendar date is a business date.

maintenance._schedule: CDE job rsingh-evx-maintenance, cron 30 4 * * * (UTC), registered paused; cde/jobs/maintenance.py
maintenance._no_expire: tables read as a stream by another job (INTERFACES correction 3): expire_snapshots is never called on them, so no reader checkpoint can point at an expired snapshot
maintenance._gold_publish_window_utc: the nightly DAG (23:30 UTC, 4 h timeout) publishes gold inside this window; a gold table is skipped when maintenance reaches it inside the window

freshness._rule: one ref.freshness row per product and business date: the worst of its checks. batch lag = business date - last business date loaded (business days; from ref.load_audit COMMITTED rows of the table's stage, or max(date_col) when given); stream lag = end of the business date (UTC) - latest event time (minutes); GREEN within the SLA, AMBER within SLA + amber_extra, RED beyond or never loaded; tables that do not exist yet are skipped

field._bronze: telematics and DTC reach bronze as streams on the live dates (no batch file), so their bronze tables are stream checks

late_data._rule: an EDR dump is late when it lands on or after business date E + ceil(sla_hours / 24), E being its event date (IST date of trigger_ts): by then the 72 h counted from the start of E have passed. The arrival time inside a day is not known, only the landing date.
